rationale: No candidate contains a concrete, material drafting template for the brief acceptance telegram. C10 is the closest in combining diplomatic pleasantry, anticipated personal contact, and pleasure language, while C19 and C08 share the formal address-and-signature format of a presidential telegram. These similarities are generic diplomatic correspondence conventions rather than distinctive shared wording, a parallel operative sequence, or adapted administrative machinery.

shared_material.child_excerpt: It gives me great pleasure to confirm my acceptance of your gracious invitation to attend the meeting of Presidents
shared_material.parent_excerpt: It always gives me the greatest pleasure to welcome you to Washington and to have an opportunity of seeing you again. I am looking forward to seeing you
shared_material.explanation: C10 shares pleasure language and anticipation of a presidential meeting, but its purpose is welcoming an arriving visitor rather than accepting an invitation, and the wording is conventional.

shared_material.child_excerpt: His Excellency ... President of the Republic of Panama ... DWIGHT D. EISENHOWER
shared_material.parent_excerpt: His Excellency ... President of the Republic of Guatemala ... DWIGHT D. EISENHOWER
shared_material.explanation: C19 shares the formal diplomatic telegram layout, but that layout is routine boilerplate and its substantive language does not match.

shared_material.child_excerpt: His Excellency ... President of the Republic of Panama ... DWIGHT D. EISENHOWER
shared_material.parent_excerpt: His Excellency ... President of the Republic of Lebanon ... DWIGHT D. EISENHOWER
shared_material.explanation: C08 likewise shares only the standard address, compact message, and signature structure of diplomatic telegrams.
